Subject: Clarification on breach notification timing and cooperation clause

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Before our procurement team moves forward, legal has asked us to confirm a couple of items in the DPA around incident response. Two specific asks:

1) What is Redwood's committed timeline for notifying customers after you detect an unauthorized access to customer data (we're looking for language like "without undue delay" but with a concrete SLA if possible)?
2) We need explicit cooperation language regarding investigations and regulator engagement (e.g., Redwood will provide reasonable assistance, preserve logs for X days, and coordinate communication to affected end-users).

Can you share either the exact clause text you would accept in our DPA or point us to a template you use for customers in the healthcare space? HIPAA applicability is a concern for us.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement is targeting next week.

Best,
Marta Lopez\Security & Compliance Lead\SigmaHealth

Marta —

Thanks for the clear asks. Looping in Laura (Legal) and Priyom (Security). High level: we don’t publish a single hard SLA for "notification after detection" across all customers because investigation timelines vary, but we can commit to an initial notification within 72 hours of confirming unauthorized access affecting customer data, with ongoing updates. For healthcare customers we often add an expedited path (48 hours) and specific preservation windows for logs.

Laura — can you propose language we can put into the DPA (and include a quick description of what "confirming unauthorized access" means operationally)? Priyom — any constraints on log retention / forensic evidence we should call out (SCCs/HIPAA considerations)?

Subject: Proposed DPA language: incident notification & cooperation

Marta —

Thanks for the note and context. Below is proposed language Redwood is prepared to accept for inclusion in a DPA. We aim for a balance between operational realities (time to investigate and validate) and the customer's need for timely notice.

(Proposed clause)
1. Incident Notification. Redwood will provide Customer with initial written notice of any confirmed Security Incident that affects Customer Data within seventy-two (72) hours of Redwood’s confirmation that an incident impacting such Customer Data has occurred. The initial notice will include: (a) a summary of the nature of the Security Incident; (b) the types of Customer Data reasonably believed to be affected; (c) the date(s) of occurrence or discovery; and (d) the remedial steps taken to date. Redwood will provide follow-up notices as material information becomes available and a final report when the investigation is concluded.

2. Cooperation and Regulatory Support. Upon Customer’s request, Redwood will reasonably cooperate with Customer (or Customer’s designated counsel) in investigating the Security Incident, including (i) providing relevant logs and forensic artifacts maintained by Redwood, (ii) preserving such records for a period of at least ninety (90) days (or longer as required by applicable law), and (iii) making Redwood personnel available for reasonable interviews or depositions. Redwood will take commercially reasonable steps to support Customer’s communications with regulators and impacted individuals, subject to Redwood’s obligations to protect third-party confidentiality and law enforcement requests.

3. HIPAA/Addendum. For Customers that are covered entities or business associates under HIPAA, Redwood will reasonably cooperate to provide the information required for Customer to meet its notification obligations; however, Customer remains responsible for determining whether and when notice to individuals or HHS is required.

4. SCCs / Cross-border. Redwood acknowledges contractual obligations arising from SCCs or other transfer mechanisms and will cooperate to assist with regulator requests tied to cross-border incidents.

Attachments included: a redline-friendly Word doc with the same language, an excerpt showing where we map this language to our SOC 2 controls, and a short text file that cites commonly requested DPA excerpts (SCC references). Please find them attached.

If you want minor edits (e.g., shorten the initial notice to 48 hours for SigmaHealth given your healthcare needs), we can take that request to our Risk Committee for approval — please let us know.

Regards,
